description: Simulates the Slack Web API including chat, conversations, users, reactions, pins, files, and more. Every method answers GET and POST, and arguments are accepted as a query string, a form body, multipart, text/plain or JSON, as Slack accepts them. A name that is not a method answers unknown_method before authentication, and every error repeats its code in the x-slack-failure header. The caller is identified from the token, which may be sent in the Authorization header or a form body field: any well-formed xoxb-, xoxp- or xapp- token is accepted, seeded tokens speak for their own user, and auth.revoke revokes. api.test answers without a token. conversations.list, conversations.history, conversations.replies, conversations.members, users.list and users.conversations page with a cursor and a limit, with next_cursor empty on the last page, invalid_cursor for a cursor that does not compute, and an unusable limit adjusted. Empty lists are answered as [], never null. A state snapshot keeps every store, including pins, bookmarks, usergroups, presence, deleted messages and the ts counter. The external file upload runs end to end on the emulator: files.getUploadURLExternal returns an upload URL on the host the client called, the bytes are posted there, and files.getUploadURLExternal requires filename and length, files carry a mimetype and filetype taken from the extension, and files.completeUploadExternal posts a file_share message, with initial_comment as its text and thread_ts honoured, to each channel in channel_id or channels and emits it as a message event. files.list filters by channel, user, types, ts_from and ts_to. views.publish keeps one Home tab view per user, replaced on each publish and guarded by its hash, and views.update finds a view by view_id or external_id; views.open and views.push keep the modal they open, without checking trigger_id. oauth.v2.access is called without a token, takes the client credentials by HTTP Basic or as arguments, and exchanges any authorization code once for a new bot token that the rest of the API accepts. conversations.open resumes the existing direct or multi-person message for the same users, answers a direct message with a D id that names the other user, and returns only the channel id unless return_im is set. Reactions and pins belong to the caller, a message is pinned once, and reactions, pins and bookmarks answer channel_not_found for a channel that does not exist; bookmarks.add takes a link bookmark with a title and an http or https URL, bookmarks.edit refuses a link that is not a URL with invalid_link, and bookmarks.edit and bookmarks.remove answer not_found for a bookmark that is unknown or in another channel. conversations.join on a channel the caller is already in answers ok with the warning already_in_channel and response_metadata.warnings. chat.postMessage reflects username, icon_emoji as icons.emoji, attachments, metadata and reply_broadcast, and chat.getPermalink answers message_not_found for an unknown ts. users.setPresence answers invalid_presence for anything but auto or away. A handler given a JSON body that does not parse answers invalid_arguments. conversations.list and users.conversations list public channels by default and filter by types, and list a private channel, direct message or multi-person message only to its members. conversations.history and conversations.replies answer channel_not_found for a channel that does not exist, and replies answers thread_not_found for a ts that is not a message in the channel. A user group always carries is_usergroup: true, a disabled group carries its date_delete, and usergroups.list leaves disabled groups out unless include_disabled is set. With a Request URL set through --webhook-url or POST /admin/events/config, chat.postMessage, chat.delete and reactions.add are delivered as Events API event_callbacks, and conversations.join, invite, leave and kick as member_joined_channel and member_left_channel, signed with X-Slack-Signature over v0:{timestamp}:{body}; a delivery that fails is retried up to three times with x-slack-retry-num and x-slack-retry-reason unless the receiver answers x-slack-no-retry: 1. Setting the Request URL through POST /admin/events/config makes Slack's url_verification handshake, and POST /admin/reset clears the delivery log and queued events. Messages, edits, channels, topics, purposes, files, memberships, profiles and presence belong to the user the token speaks for, and a channel's is_member says whether that user is in it.
